newsitem.title: ROMANIA: LANDSLIDES, FLOODS HIT THOUSANDS OF ROMANIA HOMES.
newsitem.headline: LANDSLIDES, FLOODS HIT THOUSANDS OF ROMANIA HOMES.

text.p: Landslides and flooding caused by heavy weekend rains damaged more than 2,000 homes in foothills south of the Carpathian mountains in Romania, but no new casualties were reported, officials said on Monday.

"The situation in Prahova county is extremely difficult due more to landslides than to flooding caused by the rain at the weekend," Viorel Raicu, State secretary at the environment ministry, said by telephone.
Six people have died across Romania over the past two weeks, but the scale of the floods has been less dramatic than in Poland, the Czech Republic and Germany.
Thousands of hectares of crop land have been sumberged in western and southeast regions, but grain producing areas in central and southern Romania have been spared.
Landslides damaged more than 2,000 homes in towns and villages in Prahova and Dimbovita counties north of Bucharest, the environment ministry said.
Floodwaters had receded by Monday and workers had started to repair damaged roads and restore water and power supplies.
Authorities despatched trucks with drinking water to the worst hit area of Breaza, 160 km (100 miles) north of Bucharest, where the landslides had damaged 1,800 houses.

More rain is expected across most of Romania this week. Flood monitors kept a close eye on the Romanian section of the River Danube, whose level has been higher than normal but below flood stage over the past few days, Raicu said.
"The dikes in the area where the River Danube bends northwards, towards the (river) port of Braila, have been reinforced, but so far there is no reason for alarm," he said.
